claims.text: ONE git choke point. Every git invocation in this module goes through :func:`_git`, which raises :class:`PrimaryCheckoutWrite` if the working directory OVERLAPS the primary checkout IN EITHER DIRECTION -- it is the checkout, is under it, or CONTAINS it -- and the verb is not in :data:`READ_ONLY_REPO_VERBS`.
claims.why: Function _git is not defined in this chunk; cannot verify claim.

claims.text: Overlap is decided by file IDENTITY as well as by path text, because ``Path.resolve()`` does not canonicalise DOS-device or UNC admin-share spellings and a text-only guard was measured allowing ``git add -A`` to stage files in the checkout through them (see :func:`_overlap_reason`).
claims.why: Function _overlap_reason is imported but not defined in this chunk; claim references external function.

claims.text: The guard runs BEFORE ``subprocess`` is reached, so a mutating command aimed at the repo never executes.
claims.why: Guard implementation not present in this chunk.

claims.text: Mutating git (``add``) is only ever run with ``cwd`` set to the worktree, which lives outside the repo by construction (``GitWorktreeManager`` places worktrees under ``%LOCALAPPDATA%``).
claims.why: GitWorktreeManager is imported but not defined; worktree location not specified in this chunk.

claims.text: THE RUNNER IS NEVER TOLD WHERE THE REPO IS. :class:`RunnerContext` -- the only thing handed to injected runner/gate callables -- carries the worktree path and nothing else path-shaped. There is deliberately no ``repo_root`` field to reach for.
claims.why: RunnerContext is not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: THERE IS NO APPLY PATH. The deliverable is :class:`PatchArtifact`: inert bytes. This module defines no function that applies a patch, checks out a ref, resets, merges, or commits to the primary checkout, and :data:`READ_ONLY_REPO_VERBS` makes adding one fail loudly rather than quietly work.
claims.why: PatchArtifact is not defined in this chunk; the rest is a claim about absence of functions, which is uncheckable without full module.

claims.text: THE ONE CALLER-CHOSEN OUTPUT PATH IS FENCED. ... :meth:`TaskAttempt._persist` now clears :func:`daedalus.primary_tree.assert_write_allowed` BEFORE ``mkdir``, and a refusal is reported on the result rather than raised.
claims.why: TaskAttempt._persist is not defined in this chunk; assert_write_allowed imported but not used here.

claims.text: the SPINE LEDGER. ``SpineLedger()`` defaults to ``<repo>/runs/spine/spine.sqlite3`` (MEASURED), inside the primary checkout, and that is correct -- a durable record that an attempt happened ... It writes only under ``runs/``, never a tracked source file, so ``git status --porcelain`` is unaffected.
claims.why: SpineLedger is imported but not defined in this chunk; default path not visible.

claims.text: What this DOES write in the primary repo's ``.git``: a branch ref and a worktree registration, created by ``git worktree add -b`` via ``GitWorktreeManager``. That is how the effect becomes findable after a crash. HEAD does not move, no tracked file changes, and ``git status --porcelain`` stays byte-identical -- which the test suite asserts after every scenario.
claims.why: GitWorktreeManager imported; no code in chunk to verify claims about git worktree add or test assertions.

claims.text: FAILURE IS A STATE, NOT AN EXCEPTION ... :meth:`TaskAttempt.run` returns an :class:`AttemptResult` in every case. The states: ...
claims.why: TaskAttempt.run and AttemptResult not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: ``no_change`` and ``cancelled`` are additions to the five states the brief named.
claims.why: No 'brief' reference in chunk; claim about additions cannot be verified.

claims.text: ``no_change`` exists because gates run against an UNMODIFIED tree are a vacuous pass: without this state a runner that did nothing returns ``clean``, which is exactly the kind of unearned green this project forbids. Gates are skipped in that state -- there is nothing to judge.
claims.why: No code in chunk showing gate skipping or state transition logic.

claims.text: LEDGER RESOLUTION ... The recorded intent is "produce a candidate patch", so it is COMPLETED whenever an artifact exists -- including ``gates_failed`` ... ``effect_id`` is the patch digest. Intents are marked FAILED only when no artifact was produced at all.
claims.why: Ledger resolution logic not in this chunk.

claims.text: ``shutil.disk_usage`` raises on a missing path, so checking the worktree root directly would report ``storage_unavailable`` on a first run purely because the directory has not been created yet. Walking up asks the question that was actually meant: does the VOLUME have room -- and it asks it without creating anything, so the storage check stays side-effect free.
claims.why: nearest_existing (aliased) not defined in chunk; claim about its behavior unverifiable.

claims.text: A token that raises is treated as "not cancelled": a broken token must not be able to abort work it was only supposed to observe.
